This page is generated from the control plane's OpenAPI 3.1.0 description (`GET /api/v1/openapi.json`, committed as `docs/openapi/weavesignal-v1.json` in the repository), so it cannot drift from the routes: `just openapi` writes it and `just ci` fails when it is out of date.
Who may call a route, how a refusal looks and what the API promises are in [Control plane routes](/docs/reference/control-api/).

## Routes: station

The station, and whether the service is alive.

### GET /api/v1/openapi.json

**The API's description**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

This document: the API as OpenAPI 3.1, generated from the handlers. Needs no bearer; the description is not secret.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | This document, OpenAPI 3.1. | any |

### GET /api/v1/station

**The station**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

The station's identifier and its name in force: the one set on the setup page, else the settings file's (ADR-0237).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The station. | [Station](#schema-station) |

### GET /health

**Liveness**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

200 when the service and, if there is one, its database answer; 503 with `status` `degraded` when the database does not. Used by the proxy and the container healthcheck.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Alive. | [Health](#schema-health) |
| 503 | The database does not answer. | [Health](#schema-health) |

## Routes: sessions

Staff sign-in: the session tokens that open the studio's routes.

### POST /api/v1/sessions

**Sign in with a password**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

`username` and `password` for a session token (starts `rss_`). A refused sign-in answers 401 with the same sentence whether the username exists or not, after the same work.

Request body: [SignIn](#schema-signin).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | The session. | [SignedIn](#schema-signedin) |
| 401 | That username and password do not match an account here. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many tries: five failures for a username within 15 minutes, or twenty for an address. Wait for the window to pass. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/sessions/code

**Ask for an emailed sign-in code**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

A station with mail answers 202 for every username and address alike, and sends a code only to an address that belongs to that username's account when it is on, so neither the words nor the time tell a stranger who has an account. 503 when the station has no mail; 422 (`field` `email`) for something that is not an address; 429 when one address has asked ten times in ten minutes.

Request body: [AskCode](#schema-askcode).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 202 | Asked. | [CodeAsked](#schema-codeasked) |
| 422 | The request is well formed but not acceptable; the sentence names the problem, and `field` the field. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many tries: five failures for a username within 15 minutes, or twenty for an address. Wait for the window to pass. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/sessions/code/finish

**Sign in with an emailed code**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

`username`, `email` and the six-digit `code`. Any failure (unknown username, an account that is off, a wrong, used, expired or spent code) answers 401 with one sentence.

Request body: [FinishCode](#schema-finishcode).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | The session. | [SignedIn](#schema-signedin) |
| 401 | That code does not match, or has run out. Ask for a new one. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | The request is well formed but not acceptable; the sentence names the problem, and `field` the field. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many tries: five failures for a username within 15 minutes, or twenty for an address. Wait for the window to pass. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### PUT /api/v1/sessions/me/mode

**Prepare or go live**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

Sets whether this session's window is preparing a show (ADR-0276). A preparing window can look at the live desk but not drive it: the desk's commands, the carts' commands, the screener's commands, ending a pass or the show, and the station's mode are refused (409) until it is live again. Everything about the person's own show stays open. A session starts live. Answers as `GET /api/v1/sessions/me` does. The station key is always live, and so is an API token: 422.

Request body: [SetMode](#schema-setmode).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The bearer, as it is now. | [Me](#schema-me) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | The request is well formed but not acceptable; the sentence names the problem, and `field` the field. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

## Routes: studio

The studio's view: sources, callers, chat modes, notices.

### GET /api/v1/studio

**The studio's view**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key; or an API token with `studio:read`.

Sources in their slots, callers, seats, chat modes, notices, the playout link and the station mode. The studio app fetches it once and then follows `GET /api/v1/studio/events`.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The studio's view. | [View](#schema-view) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is an API token without the scope this route needs ("This API token does not hold the `…` scope."); or a staff session whose role may not do this. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### GET /api/v1/studio/events

**The studio's view as events**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key; or an API token with `studio:read`.

Server-sent events: one `state` event at once whose data is the studio view as JSON, then one per change; a keep-alive comment every 10 seconds.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | An event stream (`text/event-stream`). | string (`text/event-stream`) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is an API token without the scope this route needs ("This API token does not hold the `…` scope."); or a staff session whose role may not do this. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

## Routes: desk

The desk's switches.

### POST /api/v1/desk/commands

**A desk switch**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key; or an API token with `desk:control`.

The same requests as the desk's control socket, without `status`: `on_air`, `mute`, `cue`, `talk`, `talk_to`, or `dump` the profanity delay. Answers with the new studio view. A caller cannot go on air or in cue without their consent to record on file (409). The show on air's step switches some off (409, ADR-0271): `dump` below `callers`, the handover (the next DJ going on air) and `picture` below `full`, where the picture is held on the slate.

Request body: [DeskCommand](#schema-deskcommand).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The new studio view. | [View](#schema-view) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is an API token without the scope this route needs ("This API token does not hold the `…` scope."); or a staff session whose role may not do this. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | It does not fit the current state (or the desk refused it). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/show/end

**End the show**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

Takes everyone off air (presenters, DJs, guests, callers; callers stay in the room and the queue), fades every cart, then hands the air to automation by setting the station's mode to `auto`. When the next host's source is standing by (steady, its show next or on air by the schedule) the air passes to them instead, as a handover's two steps: they go on air as the others go off, nothing goes to automation, and `passed_to` names them. The switch waits for the profanity delay to play out, so the last words are heard; `automation_in_ms` says how long. If somebody has gone back on air by then the switch is skipped, and the studio gets a notice saying why. With no desk answering nothing is on air to take off, and the air still goes to automation. With no playout layer (`automation_in_ms` null) there is nothing to hand it to. Any staff member's, like the desk's own switches.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | What was done, and the new studio view. | [EndShowResult](#schema-endshowresult) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | It does not fit the current state (or the desk refused it). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/passes/end

### POST /api/v1/room/tokens

**A room token for one person**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

A short-lived LiveKit token for one person, with their role in it for the desk to read. A `listener` token is a monitor that hears every return (ADR-0118): only an admin may ask for one (403 otherwise). A `caller` token records the caller's consent on the station's behalf, against the words the station shows now (`consent`). A `guest`, `dj`, `screener` or `caller` token for a seat the show on air's step has switched off is refused (409, ADR-0271), unless that person is in the room already.

Request body: [TokenRequest](#schema-tokenrequest).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | The token. | [TokenResponse](#schema-tokenresponse) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is a staff session whose role may not do this: the route is admin only. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | It does not fit the current state (or the desk refused it). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | The request is well formed but not acceptable; the sentence names the problem, and `field` the field. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

## Routes: join

Invitations and the pass a guest, a remote DJ, a presenter or a caller joins by.

### POST /api/v1/invites

**An invitation link**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

A link for a guest, a remote DJ or a presenter. A caller joins another way (422). The show on air's step decides which seats can be invited (ADR-0271): below `guests` a guest or a second presenter is refused, below `full` a DJ is, each with 422 and `field` `role`; the pass is checked again when it is used. With `for_me` the invitation is a presenter's for the signed-in account, allowed at every step for the show's presenter (403 for another account at Solo, 422 for the station key); it is the Solo DJ's own microphone link. A window that is preparing a show may make it too (1.3.2): making a link is not changing what is on air.

Request body: [InviteRequest](#schema-inviterequest).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | The invitation. | [Invite](#schema-invite) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is a staff session whose role may not do this: the route is admin only. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | The request is well formed but not acceptable; the sentence names the problem, and `field` the field. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### GET /api/v1/pass

**What a pass is**

Needs: a pass, as the bearer.

The pass is the bearer: from an invitation's link or a call-in. Says who it is for and whether the studio has ended it. `not_now` says why the pass cannot join yet when the show on air runs at a step that has switched its seat off (ADR-0271); the pass stays good for later. `show_id` and `keyed` (1.3.2) say which show the invitation is for and whether that show needs a key now, for the join page's line about who will hear the guest.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The pass. | [PassInfo](#schema-passinfo) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 410 | This link has expired. Ask the station for a new one. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**A room token for a pass**

Needs: a pass, as the bearer.

Signs a token for the person's room: a caller's booth, or the studio. 410 when the studio has ended the pass or no longer has the call on file, or when the lines have closed on a caller. 409 when the show on air runs at a step that has switched this seat off (ADR-0271): the sentence says so, and the pass stays good for later. Someone already in the room is never refused.

| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | It does not fit the current state (or the desk refused it). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 410 | This link has expired, or the studio has ended it. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 500 | The token could not be signed. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### PUT /api/v1/shows/{show}

**Make or change a show**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key; or an API token with `shows:write`.

Its cards are drawn first, and a name that cannot fit, or holds characters the card fonts cannot draw, refuses the save (422, with the field named). A station with no public address (`publishing.public_url` empty) still makes and saves the show, its names checked the same way, and keeps no cards until it has one (1.2.1). The presenter's fields (`presenter`, `contact`, `links`, `commercial_music`, `presenter_account`; ADR-0214, ADR-0219) are kept as stored when the body leaves them out, so a client that does not know them never wipes a DJ's details; send an empty value to clear one. A member of staff who is not an admin may name only their own account as `presenter_account` (403 otherwise); an API token may not set it at all. Changing `presenter` or `contact` takes an admin or the show's own presenter (ADR-0241; 403 otherwise); sending them unchanged is fine. `step` (`solo`, `guests`, `callers` or `full`, ADR-0271) is kept as stored when the body leaves it out, and a new show without it starts at `solo`; changing a stored show's step takes an admin, a producer or the show's presenter (403 otherwise; an API token may not), is logged, and takes effect at once if the show is on air. `rule` (release 1.0.4, ADR-0278) is when the show airs: a value sets it, `null` clears it, and left out leaves it to `slot` (an older studio's weekly slot) as the *When it airs: the rule* reference page tabulates; the drafted episodes are not moved by this (use `PUT …/rule` for that). `draft_first: true` makes series 1 if the show has none and drafts its first episode in the same transaction (the date under way, else the next); the reply adds `drafted`, and a refusal saves nothing. A presenter (or a screener) is refused a first episode over another show's time (409, `field` `rule`, the other show named, `clashes`); an admin, a producer, the station key and a token go on and the reply carries `warnings`. Every show carries `rule`, `rule_words` and `next_on`, and `slot` while the rule is exactly a weekly slot.

| Parameter | In | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | path | string | yes | The show's slug |

Request body: [ShowInput](#schema-showinput).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|

### DELETE /api/v1/shows/{show}

**Delete a show that has never aired**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

An admin or a producer (and the station key) may; a presenter, even of their own show, a screener and an API token may not (403). Refused (409, with one sentence naming how many episodes aired) when any of its episodes has aired or is on air now: an aired show stays as the station's record. Otherwise, in one transaction, the show goes with its series, drafted episodes, own cart banks and carts, and the logs of its step and rule changes; then its card pictures, its slate still, its carts' files and any published audio files only it named are deleted from the disk, and the open cart wall is read again. A call's consent keeps the show's name in words and loses only the link to it. It cannot be undone. Past plays, the generated log and the chat name no show by its id, so they are left as they are (a clock or a log item that named one of the show's own carts is left naming a cart that is gone, as when a show's bank is removed). Release 1.0.4 (ADR-0279).

| Parameter | In | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | path | string | yes | The show's slug |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | What was deleted. | [ShowDeleted](#schema-showdeleted) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is a staff session whose role may not do this: the route is admin only. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 404 | There is no such thing. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | It does not fit the current state (or the desk refused it). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 500 | The database failed. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### PUT /api/v1/shows/{show}/rule

**Change when a show airs**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key; or an API token with `shows:write`.

Sets the show's rule alone (`null` clears it) and says what to do with the episodes already drafted for dates to come (`drafted`): `move` (the default) moves those still on their old rule dates to the new rule's dates, in order, keeping their numbers, titles and guests; `leave` leaves them. Aired episodes are never touched, and neither is an episode a person moved or made by hand. Every series that follows the show's rule is moved; one with a rule of its own is not. All in one transaction; the change is logged with who made it and every window is told. A presenter whose moved episodes would sit over another show's time is refused (409, `field` `rule`, `clashes`); others go on and the reply warns. The reply says what moved, what stayed and why.

| Parameter | In | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | path | string | yes | The show's slug |

| 403 | The bearer is an API token without the scope this route needs ("This API token does not hold the `…` scope."); or a staff session whose role may not do this. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/shows/{show}/series/{series}/episodes

**Draft episodes**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key; or an API token with `shows:write`.

The next episode, or `count` of them, filled in from the series' rule: the next dates it gives that no episode fills and it does not skip, each recorded as the date it fills (`occurrence`). With nothing drafted the first is the date under way now (its length, or an hour), else the next on or after the rule's start: never a date in the past. A rule with no more dates answers 409, and fewer than `count` are drafted when it has fewer left. A series with no rule drafts numbered episodes with no time. An episode that would overlap another show's by a minute or more is refused for a presenter (409, with `field` `rule`, the other show named and `clashes`); an admin, a producer, the station key and a token go on.

### PUT /api/v1/shows/{show}/step

**Change a show's step**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

Changes only the show's step (`solo`, `guests`, `callers` or `full`, ADR-0271), for the studio's step dialog. An admin, a producer or the show's presenter may; an API token never. The change is logged with who made it and when, every studio window is told, and if the show is the one the station's step comes from, the change takes effect at once: below `callers` call-in closes and waiting callers are released; when it rises the lines open. A person already in the room is never removed. `station` is the station's step after the change.

|---|---|---|---|---|

Request body: [StepBody](#schema-stepbody).

### POST /api/v1/schedule/import

**Make the shows chosen from a calendar file**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key; or an API token with `shows:write`.

Makes the chosen shows (1 to 200: each a name, a description and a rule, as `POST /api/v1/schedule/import/preview` proposed them or as the person renamed them) in one transaction: each a new show at step Solo, with no episode drafted and no host, in the next colours of the palette; each path made from its name and made free against the station's shows and the others in the same import, as the studio makes a new show's. Each show's cards are drawn first, and a name that cannot fit refuses the whole import (422, `field` `items[n].name`); a rule that cannot stand refuses it too (422, `field` `items[n].rule`, the item named). Nothing is made unless everything is. The reply lists the shows made and, as warnings, the dates (in the twelve months from each show's first, the first 60) where each overlaps another show's time (the others made in the same import included); an overlap never refuses the import. An admin or a producer (and the station key, and a token with `shows:write`); a presenter or a screener is refused (403). Release 1.0.5 (ADR-0281).

Request body: [ImportRequest](#schema-importrequest).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | The shows are made. | [ImportReply](#schema-importreply) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/schedule/import/preview

**Read a calendar file into proposed shows**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key; or an API token with `shows:read`.

Reads an iCalendar file (at most 1 MB and 200 events; the body is the file itself as `text/calendar`, or JSON with `ics`) and proposes one show per recurring event, and one per run of single events with the same name (on chosen dates, a date at another time moved). Each item says how it was read (`mapping`): `exact`, a rule that gives exactly the calendar's dates and times; `dates`, an RRULE no show's rule can say (every other day, the fifth Friday, another zone whose clocks change on other dates, flagged `clock_differs`), offered as its dates for the next twelve months, at most 120, with `reason`; or `refused`, with `reason` (an all-day event, a zone we do not know, more than once a day, longer than a day, every date passed). Times in another zone are converted to the station's clock. Each item carries the rule in the New show's shape, its sentence (`words`), its next dates with the other shows' times they overlap (as `POST /api/v1/schedule/rule/preview` gives them), the path it would take, and the other items it overlaps. An item that is a show the station already has (the same name with case and spaces folded, and the same dates and times still to come, as when the station's own calendar file is read back) says so in `already`, and is not counted as a clash with itself. Writes nothing. A file that cannot be read is refused (422, `field` `ics`, a sentence); a file over the limits too (413). An admin or a producer (and the station key, and a token with `shows:read`); a presenter or a screener is refused (403). Release 1.0.5 (ADR-0281).

Request body: [ImportPreviewRequest](#schema-importpreviewrequest). The file, as JSON; or the file itself with `Content-Type: text/calendar`.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The proposed shows. | [ImportPreviewReply](#schema-importpreviewreply) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is an API token without the scope this route needs ("This API token does not hold the `…` scope."); or a staff session whose role may not do this. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 413 | Larger than 1 MB, or more than 200 events. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | The request is well formed but not acceptable; the sentence names the problem, and `field` the field. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 500 | The database failed. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### GET /api/v1/schedule/rule/now

**The rule of a show that starts now**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key; or an API token with `shows:read`.

For the New show wizard's Start now (1.3.2): the one-time rule of a show that starts at the station's next whole minute and lasts `minutes` (15 to 480, 60 by default), on the station's own clock and zone, so a studio whose clock is wrong still starts it when it says. Save it as any rule (`PUT /api/v1/shows/{show}` with `draft_first: true`, which drafts the date under way): the show is on air by the schedule when the minute comes, within about three seconds, and the station's step then follows the show. The answer is for the minute it is asked in, so ask again just before saving; a rule saved up to its length late still drafts the date under way. Writes nothing.

### POST /api/v1/playout/mode

**Hand the air to automation, or take it back**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

Sets the station's mode (ADR-0045) without changing any other playout setting, and answers with the new studio view. Any staff member's: `PUT /api/v1/playout/settings` stays an admin's. Anyone on air at the desk is not taken off air; in `auto` the desk is simply not heard, and in `live` it is heard again at once. The change is immediate (profanity delay and all); End show (`POST /api/v1/show/end`) is the route that takes people off air and waits for the delay. 503 when the station has no playout layer.

Request body: [ModeRequest](#schema-moderequest).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The new studio view. | [View](#schema-view) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 500 | The database refused. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/playout/restart

**Restart playout**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

Asks playout (Liquidsoap) to shut down so that its supervisor, which every install has (Compose's restart policy, the Quadlet's `Restart=always`, the Cloudron app's supervisord), starts it again: the studio's `⌃R` pressed twice. Listeners keep their stream: the listener process holds the mount and plays its fallback until playout is back, about five seconds. Any staff member's, as the station's mode is (it changes what is on air, so a window that is preparing a show is refused with 409); an API token never reaches it. 502 when playout does not answer on its socket (it is already down, and its supervisor is starting it); 503 when the station has no playout layer.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Playout took the command. | [PlayoutRestarting](#schema-playoutrestarting) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | It does not fit the current state (or the desk refused it). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 502 | Playout did not answer on its socket. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

## Routes: public

Routes that need no bearer: the player, now playing, the feeds, the HLS files, and the open routes for a station's website (`/api/v1/public/…`, now playing), which carry CORS open to any origin and are limited per address.

### POST /api/v1/call-in

**Call the studio**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

A listener's call from the player page, with their consent to record (the words from `GET /api/v1/player`) and the answered challenge. Answers with a pass and a room token for the caller's booth. 409 (`field` `consent`) when the words have changed since the page loaded; 429 over the per-address limit.

Request body: [CallInRequest](#schema-callinrequest).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | The pass and the token. | [Joined](#schema-joined) |
| 409 | It does not fit the current state (or the desk refused it). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | The request is well formed but not acceptable; the sentence names the problem, and `field` the field. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many calls from this address just now. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 500 | The token could not be signed. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

| `limit` | query | integer | no | How many, 1 to 50. |

**The keyed shows**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

No bearer; open to any website like the other public routes, and limited per address. The shows that need a key (so the schedule and the player can show a lock), when each opens to everyone, what the public hears meanwhile, and where to get a key. It says nothing about who holds a key.

### GET /api/v1/public/schedule

**The coming schedule**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

For a station's own website: the episodes with an air time from now for `days` days, in air order. An episode that has not aired shows as its slot (show, series, number, time, length, kind, hosts); its title, description, guests and tags appear once it has aired. No person a retention rule erased appears. No bearer; CORS open to any origin; limited per address. Cached for 30 s.

| Parameter | In | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | query | integer (int32) | no | How many days from now, 1 to 14. |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The schedule. | [PublicSchedule](#schema-publicschedule) |
| 422 | The request is well formed but not acceptable; the sentence names the problem, and `field` the field. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### GET /api/v1/public/schedule.ics

**The schedule as a calendar file**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

For a person's own calendar (subscribe to it, or download it): every show with a rule, as one VEVENT each (its RRULE or RDATE, EXDATE for skipped dates, an override with RECURRENCE-ID for each moved date), in the station's zone with its VTIMEZONE, so the calendar works out the dates and the clocks changing itself. A show's rule is its current series' (that series' own start date and planned episodes win). Only the public words: the show's name and its description (its page, as `URL`, once the station serves show pages); a drafted episode's title and guests are never in it. Each show's UID is `{show id}@weavesignal` and stays the same for the show's life. `text/calendar; charset=utf-8`. No bearer; CORS open to any origin; limited per address. Cached for 30 s. Release 1.0.5 (ADR-0281).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The calendar (iCalendar, RFC 5545). | string (`text/calendar`) |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### GET /api/v1/public/shows/{file}

**One show as a calendar file**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

As `GET /api/v1/public/schedule.ics`, for one show: `{file}` is the show's path with `.ics` (`/api/v1/public/shows/the-late-kettle.ics`). A show without a rule gives a calendar with no events, so a subscription does not fail while a rule is cleared. No bearer; CORS open to any origin; limited per address. Cached for 30 s. Release 1.0.5 (ADR-0281).

| Parameter | In | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | path | string | yes | The show's path and `.ics`: `the-late-kettle.ics` |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The calendar (iCalendar, RFC 5545). | string (`text/calendar`) |
| 404 | There is no such thing. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### GET /api/v1/public/station

**The station's public facts**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

For a station's own website: the station, the show now, the stream, whether the show is live, whether call-in is open, the video, the zone. No bearer; CORS open to any origin; limited per address. Cached for 5 s.

## Routes: tokens

API tokens for integrations. Admin only.

### GET /api/v1/tokens

**API tokens**

Needs: an admin: a staff session with the `admin` role, or the station key.

| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/tokens

**Make an API token**

Needs: an admin: a staff session with the `admin` role, or the station key.

`name` (up to 80 characters), `scopes` (at least one, from the list), and `expires_in_days` (1 to 3650; left out, it does not expire). The answer carries the secret (`rsa_` and 64 hex digits) this once; the station keeps only a keyed hash of it. At most 100 live tokens (409).

Request body: [NewToken](#schema-newtoken).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | The token, and its secret, shown once. | [TokenMade](#schema-tokenmade) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is a staff session whose role may not do this: the route is admin only. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | It does not fit the current state (or the desk refused it). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | The request is well formed but not acceptable; the sentence names the problem, and `field` the field. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Revoke an API token**

Needs: an admin: a staff session with the `admin` role, or the station key.

The token stops working at once and stays in the list, marked revoked.

| `id` | path | string (uuid) | yes | The token's id. |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 204 | Revoked. |  |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is a staff session whose role may not do this: the route is admin only. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 404 | There is no such thing. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/shows/{show}/keys

**Make a show key**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

A key for one person to send to this show from their own software (ADR-0284). The reply holds the key's secret, the monitor link's secret and the details for Icecast and SRT: **shown this once**; the station keeps neither in a readable form. The show then comes from the host's own studio (`source: push`). With `hint` `pull` and a `url`, the station opens the stream itself while the slot's door is open (`source: pull`): `http://` or `https://` (Icecast or any HTTP audio in MP3, AAC, Ogg or FLAC), an HLS playlist (`.m3u8`, MPEG-TS, AAC or MP3 segments), or `srt://host:port` with any `streamid=` (the station calls the listener; MPEG-TS). The address may hold no user name, password or SRT passphrase (422). Its name is resolved when it is saved, and an address inside the station's own network is refused (422) unless the installation sets `WEAVESIGNAL_PULL_ALLOW_PRIVATE`. The reply's secret is unused for a pull; its monitor link works as any key's. For an admin, a producer or the show's presenter; an API token never.

| Parameter | In | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | path | string | yes | The show's slug |

Request body: [NewKey](#schema-newkey).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | The key, with its secrets, once. | [MadeKey](#schema-madekey) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

The desk toast's *Off air* for a source whose link was lost while it was on air (design section 3.6): its place is kept for the rules' time (`place_kept_s`), and this lets it go at once. The log says `place_let_go`, by whom. The tile leaves the stage, and if the source reconnects it stands by instead of going back on air by itself. If nobody else is on air and the station is not on automation yet, automation takes the air first, so listeners are not left with nothing. Refused (409) unless the key's place is being kept now. For staff at the desk; an API token never.

### POST /whip/{key}

**Send from OBS over WHIP**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

WHIP (RFC 9725) for a host's own software (17d): the body is an SDP offer (`application/sdp`) and the bearer is the show key's secret (OBS's *Bearer Token*; `<key id>-<secret>` is taken too). The reply is `201` with the SDP answer and the session's address in `Location`. The station answers ICE-lite with one host candidate, its public IPv4 address and its WHIP port (`ports.source_whip`, UDP, off unless the installation turns it on), and takes the Opus sound only: a picture the software sends is received and discarded, so OBS needs no change. From there the source is a host's own studio like Icecast and SRT (ADR-0280): standing by in its show's slot, a private test outside it, refused with a wrong key (five wrong keys from an address in a minute refuse it for ten minutes). No trickle ICE.

| Parameter | In | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | path | string | yes | The show key's id (8 characters) |

Request body (`application/sdp`): string. The SDP offer.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 201 | The SDP answer; `Location` is the session's address. | string (`application/sdp`) |
| 400 | The offer has no Opus sound, or is not one the station can read. | string (`text/plain`) |
| 401 | No bearer, or the wrong key. | string (`text/plain`) |
| 403 | Refused: not the key's slot with tests off, the key ended, or turned away. | string (`text/plain`) |
| 409 | Another connection is using this key. | string (`text/plain`) |
| 413 | The offer is over 32 KB. | string (`text/plain`) |
| 415 | Not `application/sdp`. | string (`text/plain`) |
| 429 | Too many wrong keys from this address. | string (`text/plain`) |
| 503 | WHIP is off at this station, or the ingest or the desk is busy or away. | string (`text/plain`) |

### DELETE /whip/{key}/{session}

**End a WHIP session**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

The host's software ends its WHIP session (the address `Location` gave), with the same bearer as its offer: the source ends as when Icecast or SRT disconnects.

| Parameter | In | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | path | string | yes | The show key's id |
| `session` | path | string | yes | The session, from `Location` |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Ended. |  |
| 401 | No bearer, or the wrong key. | string (`text/plain`) |
| 404 | No such session: it has ended already. | string (`text/plain`) |
| 503 | WHIP is off at this station. | string (`text/plain`) |

## Routes: monitor

A host's monitor link (ADR-0280): their own source's state and the station's clock, and a listen-only room token for the sound of the programme without them. The bearer is the monitor secret from the key's making; it needs no account.

### GET /api/v1/monitor

**The monitor link's view**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

What the host behind a monitor link sees: their own source's state (`on_air`, `open`, `standby`, `link_lost`, `test`, `not_connected`) and the lamp's sentence, what happens next with the instant it counts to (`then.at_ms`, on the station's clock), the post (the grace, a hold, the late count) as far as it is theirs, before you, you and after you, the next insert as far as the log can say, the show's step, the next host, the last refusal in words, what the station hears of them, and what they may press now (`controls`, each with `why_not`). The bearer is the monitor secret from the key's making; it needs no account. 401 for a secret that is not one; 410 when the key has ended; 429 for too many wrong secrets from one address.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The host's own view. | [MonitorView](#schema-monitorview) |
| 401 | Not a monitor link's secret. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 410 | The key has ended. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

## Routes: internal

Routes for the station's own processes on the same machine; never reachable through the proxy.

### POST /api/v1/internal/sources/admit

**May this connection stand by?**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

For the ingest on this machine only, before it reads any media. With the key id (and, for Icecast, the secret; for a pull, way `pull` and no secret) and the address: `standby` with the desk slot promised to it, `test` (outside its slot, never on the desk) with how long, or `refused` with its reason. For SRT the reply carries the passphrase for the handshake; the handshake's outcome comes back on `events`. Five wrong keys from a public address in a minute refuse it for ten minutes; an address that is private, loopback, link-local or carrier-grade NAT is counted and logged but never refused.

Request body: [AdmitRequest](#schema-admitrequest).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The decision. | [AdmitReply](#schema-admitreply) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is a staff session whose role may not do this: the route is admin only. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

## Routes: rehearsal

The rehearsal studio (1.3.0): a second desk with no way to the air, for one show at a time. A person's, never an API token's.

### GET /api/v1/rehearsal

**The rehearsal studio**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

Whether this station has a rehearsal studio, its desk's link, the open session (one show at a time), the people at the rehearsal desk and the carts sounding there. Nothing in the rehearsal studio reaches the air. `may_run` says whether the asker may run the open session. The studio app fetches it once and then follows `GET /api/v1/rehearsal/events`.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The rehearsal studio. | [RehearsalView](#schema-rehearsalview) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### GET /api/v1/rehearsal/bookings

**The rehearsal studio's bookings**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key; or an API token with `schedule:read`.

Every booking of the rehearsal studio that shares any time with the stretch asked for (at most 62 days), in start order. A booking holds the studio for its show: Open for another show is refused while one does. The rehearsal studio is first come; bookings are optional. The schedule's week also gives them, with the sessions, as `rehearsals`. For staff; an API token with `schedule:read`.

| `from_ms` | path | integer (int64) | yes | From, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. |
| `to_ms` | path | integer (int64) | yes | To (exclusive); at most 62 days after `from_ms`. |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The bookings. | [BookingList](#schema-bookinglist) |
| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is an API token without the scope this route needs ("This API token does not hold the `…` scope."); or a staff session whose role may not do this. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | The request is well formed but not acceptable; the sentence names the problem, and `field` the field. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/rehearsal/bookings

**Book the rehearsal studio**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

Books the rehearsal studio for one show from `start_ms` until `end_ms`: 201 and the booking. From now on (a minute's slack), at least five minutes and at most a day (422 naming the field). Bookings never share time: one that would is 409, with the sentence and the booking in the way (`clash`); one that starts as another ends does not share time. Whoever may change the show's step may (its presenter, a producer, an admin, the station key); 403 otherwise. 503 when the station has no rehearsal studio or no database.

### POST /api/v1/rehearsal/move

**Move to the live studio**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key.

Moves everyone in the rehearsal studio to the live studio, on the links they already have, and closes the session. In order: the move is written on the session (who moved, and the opening state: who is on and who is muted at the rehearsal desk, among the people present); each person's page is sent a live pass on `GET /api/v1/pass/events` (`move`), and joins the live room **standing by**: nobody goes on air until the handover; then the session ends, so its rehearsal links buy nothing more. The opening state is applied when the show's host is put on air at the live desk, by whichever route (the schedule, the handover's press, taking the air from automation, their own On key): the muted are muted, then the others who were on are put on air with the rules' fade. 409 with no session open, with nobody in the rehearsal studio, or when the show has no airing under way or within twelve hours (the sentence says so). Whoever may run the session's show (403 otherwise), from a live or a preparing window.

| 401 | No bearer, a wrong one, or a staff session that has ended ("Your sign-in has ended. Sign in again."). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The bearer is a staff session whose role may not do this: the route is admin only. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### GET /api/v1/listener-keys/leaks

**The leak report**

Needs: staff: any staff session, or the station key; or an API token with `keys:manage`.

A producer, an admin, or an API token with `keys:manage`. For each key (of a family, or all): first and last seen, listens, devices, distinct addresses (ever, in 24 hours, in seven days), the most new addresses in one hour (`spike` from 3), and a `score` with its `reasons` for "most likely passed on", sorted highest first. An address is never shown, only counted (the station keeps a keyed hash of it for `keys.use_records_days`).

## Routes: listen

Keyed shows, the listener's side: entering a key for a signed token, renewing it, the devices that hold a key, and a lost key. No bearer; the key is the credential.

### POST /api/v1/keyed/devices

**The devices that hold a key**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

No bearer: the key is the credential. The browsers and apps that have used it, the live ones first, so a holder who is told the key is in use on its most devices can sign one out. Wrong keys are counted like a redeem's.

Request body: [ListenDevices](#schema-listendevices).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The devices. | [ListenDeviceList](#schema-listendevicelist) |
| 404 | No such key (`not_recognised`). |  |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Sign a device out of a key**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

No bearer: the key is the credential. The device is refused at its next renewal and its place is free at once. 404 for a key not recognised or a device the key does not have.

Request body: [ListenDeviceEnd](#schema-listendeviceend).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 204 | Signed out. |  |
| 404 | No such key or device. |  |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/keyed/lost

**Ask for a lost key**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

No bearer. The station emails the key's link to the address if a key was made with it, and says the same thing whether one matched or not (`202`), so the route cannot be used to find out who has a key. The work is done after the answer, so it takes the same time either way. Limited per address (`keys.lost_per_hour`, 429) and per email address (further requests are answered the same and send nothing). With mail off, nothing is sent and the request is logged on the matching keys (`lost_key_asked`) for staff to send the key themselves.

Request body: [ListenLost](#schema-listenlost).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 202 | Always, within the limits: `{ message, mail }`. `mail` says whether the station sends email (the message follows it: with mail off the request is for staff to answer, and the screen should say so). It is about the station, never about the address, so it is the same whether a key matched or not. | [ListenLostAnswer](#schema-listenlostanswer) |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/keyed/redeem

**Enter a key**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

No bearer: the key is the credential. `key` is the text as typed or sent (case, dashes and spaces are ignored); `show` the show wanted (id or slug), if any; `device` this browser's id from last time, if it has one. The answer is a signed token for one show's window (`show`: the one named, else the keyed show on now that the key opens, else the next one; from `starts_ms` to `expires_ms`), the keyed addresses with the token in their path (`urls`), the device's id to keep, and what the key is, for the welcome. Renew about every `renew_in_s` seconds: the renewal is the device's place on the key. A refusal carries a `code` and a plain sentence: `not_recognised` (404), `not_yet_valid` (403, with `from_ms`), `ended` (403, `until_ms`), `paused`, `revoked`, `does_not_open_show`, `not_scheduled` (403: none of its shows has a keyed window on the schedule in the next fortnight), `too_many_devices` (409, with the `devices` that hold it), `people_limit`, `listens_used_up` (409). Redeems are limited per address per minute, and wrong keys per address per ten minutes (429).

Request body: [ListenRedeem](#schema-listenredeem).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The token and the key. | [ListenToken](#schema-listentoken) |
| 403 | The key is known but does not open now: `code` says why. |  |
| 404 | No such key (`not_recognised`) or no such show. |  |
| 409 | A limit of the key is reached (`code` says which). |  |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### POST /api/v1/keyed/renew

**Renew a key's token**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

No bearer: the token is the credential. Trades a token that has not ended for a fresh one for the same show (its window now, or its next), after re-reading the key: a key revoked, paused, ended, signed out or no longer opening the show is refused here (the same `code`s as redeeming, and `device_signed_out`; 403 or 409). A revoked or paused key is also refused at once by the station and its edges, whatever its token's life. A renewal does not count as a listen and never makes a device. A token that has ended is `401` (`token_ended`): redeem the key again. Limited per device.

Request body: [ListenRenew](#schema-listenrenew).

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The fresh token. | [ListenToken](#schema-listentoken) |
| 401 | The token is not valid or has ended (`token_ended`, `token_invalid`). |  |
| 403 | The key no longer opens: `code` says why. |  |
| 409 | A limit of the key is reached. |  |
| 429 | Too many requests just now: per address on the open routes, per API token elsewhere. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### GET /api/v1/keyed/revoked

**Keys revoked or paused lately**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

No bearer: for edges (`EDGE_KEYED_REVOKED_URL`), which read it every half-minute or so and refuse these keys' tokens at once, and end their streams. `{"revoked": [key ids]}`: every key revoked or paused within two days (longer than any token lasts). Ids only, never a name or a key's text.

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The ids. | any |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### GET /hls/k/{show}/{token}/{path}

**A file of a keyed show's HLS**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

No bearer: the token in the path is the credential (`ks1.…`, from redeeming a key). Checked on every playlist and segment: its signature, its time, the show, and the medium (`audio.m3u8` and `audio/…` need sound, the rest video); a key revoked or paused is refused at once. Serves the public segments and this show's, never another keyed show's (each segment is judged by when it was written against the times the public gate was shut). Answers `Cache-Control: private`. 403 with a `code` when refused; 404 while video is off.

| Parameter | In | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | path | string | yes | The show's id, as the token names it |
| `token` | path | string | yes | The token |
| `path` | path | string | yes | A playlist or segment, such as `live.m3u8` or `audio/seg1.m4s` |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The file. | [File](#schema-file) (`application/vnd.apple.mpegurl`) |
| 403 | The token does not open this file now (`code` says why). |  |
| 404 | There is no such thing. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### GET /listen/k/{show}/{token}/{mount}

**A keyed show's stream**

Needs: nobody (no bearer).

No bearer: the token in the path is the credential, and it must open sound. `mount` is `programme-keyed.opus` or `programme-keyed.mp3` (when the MP3 stream is on). Only while the show's window is open (with its margins). The stream is the keyed programme from the listener process, carried by the control plane so that it can end it: at once when the key is revoked or paused, when the token ends, and when the show's window closes. 403 with a `code` when refused.

| Parameter | In | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | path | string | yes | The show's id, as the token names it |
| `token` | path | string | yes | The token |
| `mount` | path | string | yes | `programme-keyed.opus` or `programme-keyed.mp3` |

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | The stream, until it is ended. | any (`audio/ogg`) |
| 403 | The token does not open this stream now (`code` says why). |  |
| 404 | There is no such thing. | [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | The part of the station that answers is not configured or does not answer (the desk, the database, LiveKit, mail). | [Problem](#schema-problem) |

### Schema: AdmitRequest

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | yes | The address the connection came from, as the ingest saw it (for the bridge, the station's proxy's last `X-Forwarded-For` entry). |

| `key_id` | string | yes | The key id the host's software gave (the SRT stream id, or the Icecast password's first part). |
| `secret` | string, or null | no | The secret it gave, for Icecast and WHIP; left out for SRT, whose handshake proves it, and for a pull, which the station opened itself. |
| `stream` | string, or null | no | For `vban`: the stream's name, which with the address must be bound to the key. |
| `way` | string | yes | `icecast`, `srt`, `whip`, `bridge` (the studio app's WebSocket), `vban`, or `pull`. A pull's key is admitted only as `pull`, and only a pull's key is. |

### Schema: CartCommand

What the studio app asks of the wall (`POST /api/v1/carts/commands`).

One of:

- **`op` is `toggle`**. A cart's key: fire it, or fade it out if it is sounding (keymap section 4).


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cart` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

- **`op` is `fire`**


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cart` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

- **`op` is `stop`**


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cart` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

- **`op` is `stop_last`**. `Space`: fade out the cart started last.

- **`op` is `fade_all`**. `⇧Space ⇧Space`: fade out everything sounding.

- **`op` is `cue`**. `⇧` and a cart's key: cue it into the presenters' ears, or take it out of the cue.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cart` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

- **`op` is `clear_cue`**. `Esc`: take every cued cart out of the cue.

- **`op` is `talk`**


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity` | string | yes |  |
| `on` | boolean | yes |  |

- **`op` is `talk_to`**


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity` | string | yes |  |
| `on` | boolean | yes |  |
| `to` | string | yes |  |

- **`op` is `dump`**. Dump the profanity delay (`Del Del`): listeners jump to the live programme, and the delay builds back up. Allowed while it rebuilds; refused only when nothing is held.

- **`op` is `picture`**. Who chooses the picture (video on): `auto` follows the audio, `slate` holds the slate (the desk's F7), `person` holds one camera.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity` | string, or null | no |  |
| `mode` | string | yes |  |

- **`op` is `caption`**. A line over the picture for `ms` (a featured chat message); `text` empty takes it down.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ms` | integer (int32) | no |  |
| `text` | string, or null | no |  |

- **`op` is `now_playing`**. The slate's text (ADR-0010), from what playout says is playing.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `artist` | string, or null | no |  |
| `show` | string, or null | no |  |
| `station` | string, or null | no |  |
| `title` | string, or null | no |  |

- **`op` is `mode`**. The station's mode (ADR-0045): in auto mode the video's sound is playout's feed whoever is live at the desk (ADR-0172). Sent when the desk's status says another.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [StationMode](#schema-stationmode) | yes |  |

### Schema: GpuFacts

A graphics card the desk could encode the station's video on (NVENC), as the install knows it (1.2.1, ADR-0292): that a card is there, not its model, so not whether it has the AV1 encoder the station's video needs (the desk falls back to the CPU where it has not). The studio's Settings offers a card that is there and not in use; nothing turns one on but the settings file's `GPU=nvidia`, set by a person, and an update never does.

| `in_use` | boolean | yes | Whether the desk has been handed the card (`GPU=nvidia`): the setting, not a reading of the desk. With video on it then encodes on the card what the card takes, and the rest on the CPU; the desk's log says which. |
| `video` | boolean | yes | Whether video is on (`VIDEO=true`): a card encodes nothing without it. |

The outgoing Icecast source (ADR-0226): the programme sent to another Icecast server as a source, for a DJ's AzuraCast. The listener process holds the connection and says how it is doing (`icecast_out.status`); the control plane decides when it sends. The remote password is never in here.

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bitrate` | integer (int32) | yes | Constant MP3 bit rate, kbit/s. |
| `bytes_sent` | integer (int64) | yes | Counted from the stream's constant bit rate while connected, since the listener process started; not read from the socket. |
| `configured` | boolean | yes | The deployment sends to a server and has its password (`ICECAST_OUT` in the settings). Everything below is empty when it is false. |
| `connected` | boolean | yes | The remote server accepted the login and takes the stream. |
| `connected_since_ms` | integer (int64), or null | no | When the current connection was made, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. |
| `failures` | integer (int32) | yes | Failed tries in a row; the pause between tries grows from 5 s to 30 s. |
| `host` | string | yes |  |
| `last_error` | string | yes | The last error, in words; kept after a reconnect, with its time. Empty if none yet. |
| `last_error_at_ms` | integer (int64), or null | no |  |
| `mode` | [IcecastOutMode](#schema-icecastoutmode) | yes | The station's choice: `auto` (while live with the desk on air), `on` or `off`. |
| `mount` | string | yes |  |
| `port` | integer (int32) | yes |  |
| `reason` | string | yes | Why, in words: "live with the desk on air", "off", and so on. |
| `tls` | boolean | yes |  |
| `wanted` | boolean | yes | The control plane is asking the listener process to send now. |

### Schema: KeyedOnAir

A keyed show's window, as the desk's Playout panel tells it (1.3.2).

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `confirmed` | boolean | yes | Playout itself answered at the last look (1.3.2). False while playout does not answer: then `kept` and `public_hears` are what the listener process's fallback does by design, not something playout said, and the studio words them as "not confirmed". True whenever playout answered, whatever it said. |
| `kept` | boolean | yes | Playout's public gate is shut, as playout itself answered at the last look (every two seconds), or playout is away and the listener process plays its own fallback: either way the public stream does not carry the show. False is the studio's alarm: playout refused, has keyed shows off, or does not know them. |
| `public_hears` | string, or null | no | What the public stream plays meanwhile, as playout says: `slate_file` (the station's `keyed.slate`), `fallback` (its fallback files), `default_loop` (the loop WeaveSignal ships) or `silence`; `listener_fallback` while playout is away; `null` when it does not say (an older playout script) or the gate is not shut. |
| `show` | string (uuid) | yes | The keyed show whose window is open (with its margins). |

### Schema: ListenerDelay

The listener delay the surfaces show (ADR-0103, ADR-0165, ADR-0272): the parts that are read live, and the rest as the station's setting. What is read live is the profanity delay (the desk reports it) and what the listener process holds of playout's feed (its own `feed.buffer_length`). What is not: the listener process's mount holds back a fixed stretch before it serves listeners, and each listener's player buffers on top. No marker travels in the stream (a metadata change would chain the Ogg stream and drop the mount, AGENTS.md), so there is no measurement from the desk to a listener's ear; `measured` says whether there is one.

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `basis` | [DelayBasis](#schema-delaybasis) | yes | `estimate` while `set_ms` is not 0; `measured` only when the whole path was measured (issue 17). The same fact as `measured`, as a word a client can show. |
| `desk_ms` | integer (int64) | yes | How much the desk's profanity delay holds now (read live from the desk), to 0.1 s. |
| `measured` | boolean | yes | True only when no part of `ms` is a setting. Nothing measures the mount's hold or a player's buffer, so it is false in this build; the app words the figure as an estimate and names the parts that are read. |
| `mount_hold_ms` | integer (int64), or null | no | Of `set_ms`, the listener mount's own hold (fixed, 12 s; not a setting); `null` when the station gives the older single figure (`studio.listener_delay_ms`), which cannot be split (ADR-0289). |
| `ms` | integer (int64) | yes | The total: `desk_ms` plus `process_ms` plus `rest_ms`. |
| `player_ms` | integer (int64), or null | no | Of `set_ms`, what a listener's player is taken to add (`studio.player_allowance_ms`); `null` with the older single figure. While the listener process's buffer is not read, `set_ms` also holds its nominal 0.5 s, so the parts do not always add up to it. |
| `process_ms` | integer (int64), or null | no | How much of playout's feed the listener process holds now (read live from it, to 0.1 s); `None` while it does not answer. |
| `read_ms` | integer (int64) | yes | The part of `ms` that is read live now: `desk_ms` plus `process_ms` (the latter 0 while the listener process does not answer). |
| `rest_ms` | integer (int64) | yes | The rest of the path as the settings say it (the mount's fixed 12 s and `studio.player_allowance_ms`, or the older `studio.listener_delay_ms`): the mount's own hold, playout and a listener's player. Never read. |
| `set_ms` | integer (int64) | yes | The part of `ms` that is a setting and never read: the same as `rest_ms`. |

### Schema: Opening

The opening state a move carries (section 1.6): who is on and who is muted, applied when the show's host is put on air at the live desk, never on arrival. `cue`, `talk` and `talk_to` are momentary and are not carried; there are no levels to carry.

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `airing_end_ms` | integer (int64), or null | no | The airing's end, in ms since the Unix epoch: a page that missed the move is offered it again until then, and an opening never applied lapses then. |
| `airing_start_ms` | integer (int64) | yes | The airing the move is for: its start, in ms since the Unix epoch. |
| `applied_at_ms` | integer (int64), or null | no | When it was applied; kept until `standby_until_ms` has passed so that a live desk that starts again in between can be put right. |
| `cleared_at_ms` | integer (int64), or null | no | When it was cleared without being applied (its airing ended, or another move for the same show replaced it). A cleared opening is never applied. |
| `host` | string, or null | no | The show's host among the people moved, whose going on air applies the opening state; `None` when no host was moved (it is then applied at the first handover for the show). |
| `mute` | array of string | no | Who is muted when it is applied, before anyone is put on (sorted). |
| `on` | array of string | no | Who goes on air when it is applied (sorted). |
| `standby_until_ms` | integer (int64) | yes | Until when the moved people arrive standing by: the airing's start plus the rules' grace (`standby_until_ms`). |

### Schema: PassKind

How the pass was issued.

one of `call`, `invite`

### Schema: Period

How long one kind of record is kept.

One of:

- **`keep` is `days`**. A number of days after the record is complete (a recording ended, a call over); 0 is "not kept after the show".


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | integer (int32) | yes |  |

- **`keep` is `with_archive`**. Kept with its programme's archive and removed with it (ADR-0039's "A").

- **`keep` is `after_recordings`**. Consent: kept while any recording it covers exists, then `days` more (ADR-0107's "R+42"); until a recording is linked, it follows the logger's period.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | integer (int32) | yes |  |

- **`keep` is `with_call`**. Consent under No retention: it goes when the call's last trace does (ADR-0113).

- **`keep` is `no_limit`**. Anonymous counts only, with nothing that identifies a person (ADR-0115).

### Schema: Repeat

How a rule repeats. Weekdays are 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday).

One of:

- **`kind` is `once`**. The start date alone.

- **`kind` is `weekly`**. Every `every` weeks on these weekdays (weeks start on Monday).


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `every` | integer (int32) | yes |  |
| `weekdays` | array of integer (int32) | yes |  |

- **`kind` is `monthly_nth`**. Every `every` months on the `nth` weekday: 1 to 4, or -1 for the last.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `every` | integer (int32) | yes |  |
| `nth` | integer (int32) | yes |  |
| `weekday` | integer (int32) | yes |  |

- **`kind` is `monthly_day`**. Every `every` months on a day of the month: 1 to 31, or -1 for the last day. A month without the day is passed over.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `day` | integer (int32) | yes |  |
| `every` | integer (int32) | yes |  |

- **`kind` is `yearly`**. Every year on a date; 29 February gives leap years only.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `day` | integer (int32) | yes |  |
| `month` | integer (int32) | yes |  |

- **`kind` is `dates`**. Chosen dates.

### Schema: ScreenerCommand

What the screener (and the presenter, for a decline) does to a caller.

One of:

- **`op` is `screen`**. Open the screening conversation (the queue's selection).


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity` | string | yes |  |

- **`op` is `send`**. Send to the desk (`P`), or send again after a decline.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity` | string | yes |  |

- **`op` is `back`**. Back to the queue (`W`).


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity` | string | yes |  |

- **`op` is `decline`**. The presenter declines a caller sent to the desk (DESK BUSY).


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity` | string | yes |  |
| `reason` | string | no |  |

- **`op` is `notes`**. What the presenter reads: one line, the note, the name on air.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity` | string | yes |  |
| `line` | string, or null | no |  |
| `name_on_air` | string, or null | no |  |
| `note` | string, or null | no |  |

- **`op` is `release`**. Let a dropped caller's held place go (`⇧C`).


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity` | string | yes |  |

- **`op` is `drop`**. Drop the caller (`⌃D ⌃D`): off air, out of the room, out of the queue.


| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity` | string | yes |  |

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `role` | [StaffRole](#schema-staffrole) | yes |  |

### Schema: Then

What happens next to this host, in one sentence, with its time.

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at_ms` | integer (int64), or null | no | The instant the sentence counts to, on the station's clock (`station.now_ms`), when it counts to one. |
| `kind` | string | yes | `at_post`, `late_count`, `grace`, `held`, `waits`, `press_only`, `keeps_air`, `slot`, `link_lost`, `place_gone` or `test`: which sentence this is, for a page that picks by it. |
| `words` | string | yes | The sentence, in the design's words, without its count and without clock times: the page adds the count it draws from `at_ms` and the station's clock. |

### Schema: TokenRequest

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `booth` | string, or null | no | A listener (a monitor) for one caller's booth, by the caller's identity (ADR-0193); left out, a monitor joins the studio room. |
| `consent` | [ConsentGiven](#schema-consentgiven), or null | no |  |
| `identity` | string | yes | The person's identity in the room (rules in the reference for roles). |
| `name` | string | no | The name others see: at most 120 characters, no control characters. |
| `role` | [Role](#schema-role) | yes | One of the seven roles. |
| `subscribe` | boolean | no | Whether the token may subscribe (default yes). A native GStreamer publisher (the studio app's native path) asks for a publish-only token and listens on a second one. |
| `ttl_s` | integer (int64), or null | no | Seconds; the station's `room.token_ttl_s` when left out, and never more. |

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity` | string | yes |  |
| `role` | [Role](#schema-role) | yes |  |
| `room` | string | yes | The room it is for: a caller's booth for a caller, the named booth for a monitor that asked for one, the studio room for anyone else. |
| `token` | string | yes | The LiveKit access token. |
| `ttl_s` | integer (int64) | yes | Seconds the token can be used to join. |
| `url` | string | yes | Where browsers reach LiveKit. |

### Schema: TrunkStatus

Where the trunk stands, as `GET /api/v1/phone` shows it.

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checked_ms` | integer (int64), or null | no | When it was last made or found as made (ms since the epoch). |
| `message` | string, or null | no | Why, when it is `failed`. |
| `state` | string | yes | `making` (not made yet: LiveKit not reached, or the first try under way), `made` (the station's trunk and dispatch rule are in LiveKit, so calls reach the line) or `failed` (tried and refused; `message` says why, and it is tried again). |

### Schema: VbanIn

A VBAN stream the station takes: a sender's address and stream name, bound to a show key.

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | yes | The sender's address on the station's network (`192.168.1.20`). |
| `channels` | array of integer (int32) | no | The channels taken, left then right, counted from 1; mono is heard in both ears. |
| `key_id` | string | yes | The show key whose source it is. |
| `name` | string | yes | The stream's name as the sender sends it (Voicemeeter's `Stream1`), 1 to 16 characters. |

### Schema: VbanOut

A VBAN stream the desk sends.

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | yes | One receiver's address; never broadcast or multicast. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no |  |
| `format` | string | no | `s16` (the default; 240 frames a packet), `s24` (160) or `f32` (120, by choice only: Voicemeeter's support is not stated). |
| `name` | string | yes | The stream's name the receiver listens for. |
| `port` | integer (int32) | no |  |
| `source` | string | no | What is sent: see `OUT_SOURCES`. |

### Schema: VideoInfo

Where the player finds the HLS: `live` (AV1 with Opus) and `audio` (the same Opus alone: the audio-only toggle, ADR-0026, and older Apple devices, ADR-0024).

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | string | yes |  |
| `live` | string | yes |  |

### Schema: WeekEpisode

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `episode` | [Episode](#schema-episode) | yes |  |
| `from` | [HostFrom](#schema-hostfrom) | yes | Where its host comes from (1.3.0): `room`, at the desk, or `own`, their own studio with a show key that has not ended (ADR-0280). Worked out as the rota works it out, from the show keys standing now. |
| `resolved` | [Resolved](#schema-resolved) | yes |  |
| `series` | [Series](#schema-series) | yes |  |
| `show` | [Show](#schema-show) | yes |  |
| `studio` | string | yes | The studio column the episode is in (1.3.0): `studio`, for every show on air, wherever its host is. Shows on air share one programme, so they are never in two columns. |

### Schema: WeekEpisodes

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dates` | array of [OpenDateOut](#schema-opendateout) | yes | Every date of every show's rule in the range that no episode fills, is not skipped and is not over: what the week draws as dotted blocks, so the studio expands no rule itself. |
| `episodes` | array of [WeekEpisode](#schema-weekepisode) | yes |  |
| `public_url` | string, or null | no | The station's public address (`publishing.public_url`, without a trailing slash), where listeners reach the calendar files, the cards and the feeds; `null` when none is set. The studio builds the links it gives out from this, never from the address it talks to, which on Cloudron is behind the login (release 1.0.5, ADR-0281). |
| `rehearsals` | array of [RehearsalBlock](#schema-rehearsalblock) | yes | The rehearsal studio in the range (1.3.0): every booking, then every session (past or open; an open one ends now), each in start order. Empty when the station has no rehearsal studio. Never in the public calendar file. |
| `studios` | array of [StudioColumn](#schema-studiocolumn) | yes | The Studios view's columns, in order (1.3.0): `studio`, and `rehearsal` only when the station has a rehearsal studio. A later studio is one more entry. Absent from a station older than 1.3.0. |
| `zone` | string | yes | The zone the station's air times are read in. |

### Schema: WhipDetails

WHIP (17d), as OBS asks for it: a server address and a bearer token. Sound only.

| Field | Type | Needed | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bearer_token` | string | yes | OBS's *Bearer Token*: the secret. |
| `port` | integer (int32) | yes | The station's UDP port for WHIP's media; 0 when WHIP is off. |
| `url` | string, or null | no | `https://<public address>/whip/<key id>`, OBS's *Server*; `None` when WHIP is off or the station has no public address (its studio domain may sit behind a login). |
